statement: For $i = \sqrt{-1}$, which of the following is equal to $(3 + 2i)(1 - 4i)$?

choices.misconception: I expanded correctly to $3 - 10i - 8i^2$ but treated $i^2$ as $+1$, so I subtracted 8 instead of adding it.
I multiplied the real parts to get 3 and the imaginary parts to get $-8i$, as if complex numbers multiply part by part.
I expanded and used $i^2 = -1$, but when I combined $-12i$ and $2i$ I subtracted the 2i and got $-14i$.

hints: Multiply the two binomials as you would $(3 + 2x)(1 - 4x)$, using every pair of terms.
After expanding you will have an $i^2$ term. Replace $i^2$ with $-1$ before combining.

solutions.reliable: Expand all four products: $3 \cdot 1 = 3$, $3 \cdot (-4i) = -12i$, $2i \cdot 1 = 2i$ and $2i \cdot (-4i) = -8i^2 = 8$. Adding, the real parts give $3 + 8 = 11$ and the imaginary parts give $-12i + 2i = -10i$, so the product is $11 - 10i$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
